correctness.rationale: Independence allows at most one original in each part. For a fixed chosen original set X, independence excludes every incident subdivision vertex, and domination forces every subdivision whose endpoints are both unchosen; hence X uniquely determines D. A wholly unselected part needs a residual edge (condition 1). A unique selected original needs a selected residual edge incident to another original of its part (condition 2). The only residual-edge distance-two exception is a sole edge on two residual vertices, requiring a selected original in an endpoint part (condition 3). With at least three residual vertices a nonisolated edge shares an endpoint with a second edge, so all subdivision witnesses exist. Reconstructed these cases and independently enumerated all subsets of 25 small complete-multipartite central graphs, matching exact bivariate coefficients including K2, K3, singleton transitions. Checked the arithmetic of the stated minima for r=2, r>=3 and K_m.

value.rationale: Complete all-cardinality and original-support counting is a mathematically natural enhancement of a domination-number problem, with exact singleton-transition obstructions and minimum-attainment counts. Distinct from merely recomputing an extremal scalar; future domination-poly studies can use the coefficient formula and boundary families.

final_claim: The complete bivariate size/original-support enumerator of independent semitotal dominating sets of C(K_{n1,...,nr}) is sum over supports S obeying three stated residual conditions, with term (prod_{i in S} n_i) z^(|S|+sum_{i<j}(n_i-1_{i in S})(n_j-1_{j in S})) w^|S|; singleton-part and complete-graph boundaries included.
limitations: All graphs finite simple and r>=2; counts labelled selected subsets and not isomorphism classes.
